     COMMENTS OF AMERICAN ELECTRIC POWER SERVICE CORPORATION ON
                           THE MOTION OF
               CONSTELLATION ENERGY GENERATION, LLC

          Pursuant to Rules 212 and 2131 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal

Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”), American Electric Power Service

Corporation, on behalf of its affiliates Appalachian Power Company, Indiana Michigan Power

Company, Kentucky Power Company, Kingsport Power Company, Ohio Power Company,

Wheeling Power Company, AEP Appalachian Transmission Company, Inc., AEP Indiana

Michigan Transmission Company, Inc., AEP Kentucky Transmission Company, Inc., AEP Ohio

Transmission Company, Inc., and AEP West Virginia Transmission Company, Inc. (collectively,

“AEP”), submits these comments on the Motion to file Supplemental Comments that was filed by

Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (“Constellation”) on December 5, 2025 and in support of

the Answers filed by the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners and PJM Interconnection, LLC

(“PJM”).2

2
  The Indicated PJM Transmission Owners filed an Answer on December 8, 2025, and PJM submitted its Answer on
December 5, 2025. AEP respectfully moves for leave to file these comments out-of-time. The Commission accepts
late filings when they will aid the Commission in its decision-making process, which is the case here. See e.g., Am.
Transmission Co. LLC, 105 FERC ¶61,388 at P 12 (2003) (accepting late-filed comments because the comments
                                                                                                            (cont'd)
         AEP has experienced first-hand the rapid growth of large loads in our service territory and

recognizes the importance of enabling this development. AEP is committed to providing reliable

service, supporting economic growth, and working with all customers to determine how to best

meet their energy needs. AEP supports co-location and is cognizant of the importance of data

centers to our national security. AEP is committed to working with the Department of Energy, the

Commission, and state and regional partners to identify and implement further actions to ensure

that our nation has the energy resources and infrastructure to support America’s next generation

of innovation and industrial growth.

        Collectively, AEP is one of the largest electric utilities in the United States. We serve

approximately 5.6 million customers across our 11-state footprint, and we develop, own, operate,

and maintain the largest transmission system in North America. AEP participates in four RTOs

(PJM, SPP, MISO, and ERCOT). Our transmission system serves as the backbone in three of the

RTOs–PJM, SPP and ERCOT–and directly serves approximately 10 percent of the electricity

demand in the Eastern Interconnection, and approximately 11 percent of the electricity demand in

ERCOT. The Columbus, Ohio metropolitan area has become a major hub for data center

development and is one of the top 10 data center regions in the country.

        I.       Comments

        AEP supports co-location. If structured properly, this configuration can provide a viable

option to address the needs of certain customers, while ensuring other customers are treated fairly

in the process. Given the pace of change, every option needs to remain on the table to meet this




provide information that assists the Commission in its decision-making process). Furthermore, the comments are
being filed only a few days out-of-time, which does not cause undue prejudice or delay. See e.g., North American
Electric Reliability Corporation, 182 FERC ¶ 61094 at P 33 (2023) (granting leave to file late-filed reply comments
given interest in the proceeding and the absence of undue prejudice or delay).



                                                        2
 unprecedented demand. However, we cannot forget core principles—every customer needs to pay

for the transmission system if they are receiving service.

        The Commission should reject Constellation’s motion, which if granted would result in

affordability concerns for customers. Furthermore, this issue is already being addressed by the

Commission’s actions in other proceedings. In fact, the Motion recognizes that the subject matter

of the captioned proceedings overlaps the issues in the recently-initiated, industry-wide ANOPR

proceeding.3 A national resolution of co-location is consistent with the President’s Executive

Order which focuses on the need for development of AI infrastructure as a national, not regional,

imperative. The Commission is actively working to complete the ANOPR process by the April

30, 2026, date the Secretary of Energy has directed, and this process should drive consistent change

across the nation. For these reasons, the ANOPR proceeding is the appropriate forum to address

co-location issues.

        For the reasons stated above, FERC should reject Constellation’s Motions in this

proceeding.
